events.factual_description: AWR Music presents Yoko Shimomura's 39th Anniversary Orchestra Concert at Carnegie Hall's Stern Auditorium/Perelman Stage on January 22, 2027 at 8:00 p.m. Arnie Roth conducts the World Festival Orchestra & Chorus; Shimomura is confirmed as a composer attending, not as a billed instrumental soloist. AWR lists highlights from the Tokyo premiere across LIVE A LIVE, Legend of Mana, Xenoblade Chronicles, Super Mario RPG, FINAL FANTASY XV and KINGDOM HEARTS but explicitly warns the New York program may change.

enrichment.note: AWR Music directly links to the specific Carnegie Hall ticket event, but an October 30 check of the destination hit Carnegie Hall's web queue; no inventory, face-value price or ticket availability was verified. No exact Apple Music album/song URL verified.

sources.note: Primary presenting producer confirms January 22 date, 20:00 start, conductor, ensemble, composer's presence and explicitly non-final Tokyo repertoire examples.

sources.publisher: Carnegie Hall (ticket destination linked by AWR Music)
sources.note: Exact promoter-linked event ticket destination; direct check returned queue/safety-net failure. Availability and prices not verified.

provenance.note: Stage 1 admission: this named orchestral and choral concert is a rare live translation of Shimomura's multiple game-score worlds with the composer in attendance, not merely an anniversary logo. Stage 2 A+: make room for the specific orchestra/repertoire bridge. S/S+ rejected: touring anniversary repertoire and a composer appearance rather than one-off world premiere or a singular farewell.

en.why_it_matters: Arnie Roth and the World Festival Orchestra & Chorus trace nearly four decades of Yoko Shimomura's musical imagination from role-playing games into the concert hall, with the composer attending. The possibility of hearing her melodic language move across several game worlds, rather than a generic orchestral gaming compilation, is the reason for this specific night.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for the Carnegie Hall date if a New York trip is feasible. It is an unusually rich composer-focused program, though the anniversary tour does not make this performance a once-in-a-lifetime occasion.
en.listen_before: Yoko Shimomura — music from Legend of Mana, LIVE A LIVE and Kingdom Hearts; the listed New York program remains subject to change.

es.why_it_matters: Arnie Roth y la World Festival Orchestra & Chorus llevan casi cuatro décadas de música de Yoko Shimomura de los videojuegos a la sala de conciertos, con la compositora presente. Lo atractivo es escuchar cómo dialogan sus melodías de universos distintos, no una recopilación orquestal genérica de temas de videojuegos.
es.trip_verdict: Le haría un espacio especial a la fecha de Carnegie Hall si se arma una visita a Nueva York. El enfoque en la compositora tiene mucho peso, aunque la gira del aniversario no convierte esta función en una ocasión irrepetible.
es.listen_before: Yoko Shimomura — música de Legend of Mana, LIVE A LIVE y Kingdom Hearts; el programa anunciado puede cambiar.

events.subtitle: introducing Fujikochans 2027 — Lupin III theme's 50th anniversary
events.category: Japanese soundtrack soul and vocal-harmony crossover
events.factual_description: COTTON CLUB presents the Yuji Ohno-produced vocal group Fujikochans in a two-night return January 13–14, 2027 with sets starting 18:00 and 20:30 each night. The venue names four vocalists and two guitarists, advertises Ohno's chorus arrangements centered on the Lupin III music, and connects the engagement with the 2027 fiftieth anniversary of the Lupin III theme. Yuji Ohno is billed as producer, not as a live performer. Tickets are priced from JPY 8,500 to JPY 11,000 per person by seat category. Member web reservations begin November 3, general web November 9.

enrichment.note: Exact official reservation page was checked October 30 and explicitly reports that booking has not yet opened; dates are November 3 for JAM SESSION members and November 9 for general web booking. No live inventory or exact Apple Music link verified.

sources.note: Primary venue confirms lineup (with Ohno as producer, not listed on stage), sets, repertoire context, anniversary, charges and booking dates.
Exact booking destination confirms reservation not yet open and member/general sale dates.

provenance.note: Stage 1 admission: Yuji Ohno's four-voice Lupin arrangements, a specific two-guitar lineup, the group's first return in approximately two years, and the theme's 50th anniversary establish a live listening context. Stage 2 A+: unusually strong Japanese score/soul intersection. S/S+ rejected: four sets and continuing Lupin performances, with producer Ohno not billed to perform.

en.why_it_matters: Rather than a routine Lupin III tribute, these are Yuji Ohno's own choral arrangements sung by four formidable voices, with guitarists drawn from Lupintic Six and Zainichi Funk. Their first engagement in roughly two years arrives in the theme's fiftieth-anniversary year: a vivid junction of Japanese screen music, soul phrasing and live vocal craft.
en.trip_verdict: Prioritize one Cotton Club set if Tokyo is part of January's plans. This specific vocal lineup earns a special evening; the two-night run does not, by itself, justify traveling to Japan.
en.listen_before: Fujikochans — introducing Fujikochans with Yuji Ohno & Friends (2017).

es.why_it_matters: No es otro homenaje de repertorio a Lupin III: son los arreglos corales del propio Yuji Ohno, cantados por cuatro voces extraordinarias y con guitarristas de Lupintic Six y Zainichi Funk. El regreso del grupo tras cerca de dos años coincide con los cincuenta años del tema; un cruce muy particular entre música de pantalla japonesa, soul y oficio vocal.
es.trip_verdict: Si enero te encuentra en Tokio, sí priorizaría uno de los sets del Cotton Club. La formación amerita dedicarle la noche, pero las cuatro funciones no justifican por sí solas cruzar el Pacífico.
es.listen_before: Fujikochans — introducing Fujikochans with Yuji Ohno & Friends (2017).

events.factual_description: The Washington Ballet closes its 50th-anniversary season June 10, 2027 at Wolf Trap's Filene Center, with three works created in Washington, DC: Trey McIntyre's Blue Until June using Etta James recordings, Edwaard Liang's Wunderland to Philip Glass, and Septime Webre's Juanita y Alicia with traditional Cuban rhythms performed by a live band that has not been named. Performance starts 8 p.m. Series subscriptions are available; Wolf Trap says single tickets go on sale in early 2027. Individual ticket prices are not published on the verified page.

enrichment.note: As of October 30, the presenter says single tickets are coming in early 2027, with no direct date-specific single-ticket checkout or prices verified. No exact Apple Music listening URL verified; Etta James/Philip Glass are repertoire references, not billed live performers.

sources.note: Primary venue confirms June 10 date/time, Washington Ballet 50th-season finale, all three choreographies, Etta James/Glass score uses, and a live but unnamed Cuban band for Juanita y Alicia.

provenance.note: Stage 1 admission: live Cuban dance-band performance embedded in Septime Webre choreography alongside Etta James blues and Philip Glass and three works created in Washington offers a specific local cross-disciplinary occasion; not a general ballet-calendar listing. Stage 2 A: culturally relevant and convenient for DMV, but no exceptional new musician or one-off rarity establishes A+ or S.

en.why_it_matters: Three Washington-born choreographies form a tightly local finale: Etta James's blues phrasing, Philip Glass's pulse and, most importantly for RADAR, a live band playing Cuban rhythms for Septime Webre's Juanita y Alicia. This is a meeting of sound, movement and the city's artistic memory rather than a generic ballet gala.
en.trip_verdict: Worth marking on the local calendar for its Cuban live-music connection and its Washington story. No need to build travel plans around it; individual tickets have not gone on sale.
en.listen_before: Etta James and Philip Glass, as sonic reference points for two of the choreographies; the Cuban ensemble has not been announced.

es.why_it_matters: Tres coreografías nacidas en Washington se reúnen en un cierre muy local: el blues de Etta James, el pulso de Philip Glass y, sobre todo para RADAR, una banda en vivo con ritmos cubanos para Juanita y Alicia, de Septime Webre. Importa el encuentro entre música, movimiento y memoria cultural de la ciudad, no la etiqueta de gala.
es.trip_verdict: Vale la pena anotarlo para una salida cercana, por la música cubana en vivo y su historia washingtoniana. No hace falta organizar un viaje; todavía no se venden boletos individuales.
es.listen_before: Etta James y Philip Glass sirven de referencia para dos coreografías; los músicos cubanos aún no han sido identificados.
